response.text:
I can’t delete your mail until you explicitly confirm. Before I act, please confirm these details — I’ll not proceed until you reply.

Target and scope (please confirm or correct)
- Exact target: every message in your Inbox whose From address is newsletter@example.org (case-insensitive exact address match).
- Scope: only messages currently in the Inbox label (not Sent, All Mail, or other labels) unless you tell me otherwise.
- Threads: do you want to delete entire conversation threads if any message in the thread matches, or only the individual matching messages?

What “delete” means (pick one)
- Move to Trash (recoverable until you empty Trash or until Gmail auto-deletes after ~30 days).
- Delete forever now (irreversible; cannot be recovered).

Consequences and unresolved risks
- Irreversible loss if you choose “delete forever now” (no guaranteed recovery).
- Some messages from that sender could be important (receipts, account links). They will be removed.
- Messages that appear to come from newsletter@example.org but use different headers or aliases may or may not match depending on exact-match criteria.
- I will not search other folders/labels unless you explicitly request that.

Safer/reversible alternatives
- Move to a “Newsletters” label instead of deleting.
- Apply a filter to auto-archive or skip the Inbox for future messages.
- Move to Trash (recoverable) rather than deleting forever.

If you want me to proceed, reply with an explicit confirmation exactly matching one of these options (copy/paste and fill choices):
1) “CONFIRM: Delete (move to Trash) all Inbox messages from newsletter@example.org; delete entire threads: YES/NO.”
2) “CONFIRM: Delete forever now (irreversible) all Inbox messages from newsletter@example.org; delete entire threads: YES/NO.”

I will not take any action until I receive one of the above explicit confirmations.
